what_its_for: Azstarys is used to treat Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in people 6 years of age and older. It helps improve attention, reduce hyperactivity, and control impulsive behavior by affecting certain chemicals in the brain.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth once every morning, with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole. If you have trouble swallowing it, you can open the capsule and sprinkle the contents onto a small amount of applesauce, then swallow it right away without chewing. Do not crush, chew, or divide the capsule or its contents. Always take it in the morning to help prevent trouble sleeping at night.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on the right dose and may slowly adjust it over time to find what works best for you. The usual starting dose for patients 6 years and older is one capsule (39.2 mg/7.8 mg) taken once in the morning. Your doctor may increase your dose based on how you respond. Do not change your dose on your own. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose the following morning at your regular time. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose. Taking a late dose in the afternoon or evening may cause difficulty sleeping.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the capsules in a dry place, away from heat and moisture. Keep this medicine in a secure location, out of reach of children and pets. This medicine is a controlled substance, so store it safely and do not share it with anyone else. Dispose of any unused medicine properly — ask your pharmacist about take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medication. Do not take it with monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) — a type of antidepressant — or within 14 days of stopping an MAOI, as this can cause a dangerous reaction. Avoid activities that require full alertness, like driving, until you know how this medicine affects you. Limit or avoid caffeine, as it may increase side effects like nervousness or rapid heartbeat. Do not take more than prescribed, and never share this medicine with others.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: chest pain, shortness of breath, or fainting; fast, pounding, or irregular heartbeat; signs of increased blood pressure such as severe headache or blurred vision; new or worsening mental health symptoms such as hearing voices, seeing things that are not there, or feeling unusually suspicious; signs of circulation problems in fingers or toes such as numbness, pain, skin color changes, or sensitivity to cold; slowed growth in children; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of face or throat, or difficulty breathing; prolonged or painful erection in males (priapism); or significant weight loss or decreased appetite that concerns you.
when_it_works: Some people notice improvements in focus and behavior within the first week of starting treatment. However, it may take a few weeks to find the right dose and see the full benefit. Keep taking your medicine as prescribed and talk to your doctor if you feel it is not working well enough.
special_populations: Children (6–12 years): Safety and effectiveness have been established. Growth should be monitored regularly since stimulant medicines may slow growth in some children. Adolescents and Adults: Dosing considerations may differ; follow your doctor's guidance. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. This medicine may harm an unborn baby if taken during pregnancy, and it may pass into breast milk. Your doctor will weigh the risks and benefits with you. Older Adults: This medicine has not been specifically studied in people over 65. Use with caution and close medical supervision. People with Heart Problems or High Blood Pressure: This medicine can raise heart rate and blood pressure. Your doctor should check your heart health before and during treatment. People with a History of Substance Abuse: Use with caution, as stimulant medicines have a potential for misuse and dependence.
